html:
SMTO-EXE-0145 — The app changed before SMTO could use that button or field

GUID: 6d69135f-6cd4-5818-8713-11b65a66933a
Slug: ui-element-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO had found the button or field, but by the time it acted, the app had changed, the window had moved on or more than a minute had passed. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Avoid clicking, typing or switching windows on the Gateway's computer while SMTO is working in the app. Changing the window or moving the focus makes SMTO's earlier look at the app out of date.
  2. Ask SMTO to look at the app window again and then do the action. SMTO needs a fresh look at the app, taken less than a minute before it acts.
  3. If the app keeps redrawing itself, wait until it has finished loading before asking again. A window that is still changing outdates SMTO's view almost immediately.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next step in the task completes the action on the control you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't ask SMTO to act on a similar-looking control instead; it could change the wrong thing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A retained UI element reference was rejected because it expired after 60 seconds, belonged to another node/run/window, no longer matched the tree revision or native object, or lost required focus.

What this means

  • A retained element reference expired after sixty seconds, belonged to another node/run/window, no longer matched the tree revision/native object, or lost required focus. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A retained element reference expired after sixty seconds, belonged to another node/run/window, no longer matched the tree revision/native object, or lost required focus.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare reference ownership, age, window/tree revision and focus with a fresh exact observation.

How to fix it

  • Take a new ui.snapshot or ui.find on the same Gateway and window, review the new exact reference, then perform the action. References expire after 60 seconds and are invalidated by structural changes, window recreation, focus loss before keyboard input, ownership change or Gateway restart; the service never substitutes a similar element.
  • Take a new ui.snapshot or ui.find in the selected Gateway and window. Review the new exact reference before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Take a new ui.snapshot or ui.find in the selected Gateway and window. Review the new exact reference before another mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • A newly reviewed reference resolves to the intended current control before action.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
